To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) nonparametric duration dependence or heterogeneity is well behaved, (b) a nonparametric treatment of both is not, and (c) a simple modification of the NPMLE leads to an estimator that performs well in both cases.

(1) a parametric specification of either duration dependence or unobservable heterogeneity leads to estimators with good properties even in modestly-sized samples, (2) a nonparametric (NP) specification of both leads to estimators which exhibit large biases and which do not improve as the sample size increases, and (3) the bias in the NP specification of both features of the hazard can be substantially reduced by a simple modification to the quasiliklihood.

(a) nonparametric specifications of unobserved heteroge- neity or duration dependence, but not both, lead to well-behaved estimators, and (b) a minor modification of standard nonparametric maximum-likelihood estimation leads to a substantial improvement in the performance of the estimator when both unobserved hetero- geneity and duration dependence are specified nonparametically.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating the parameters of a nonparametric hazard model for duration data.
nonparametric estimation of duration models in which the hazard function is a function of both unobserved and observed heterogeneity and duration dependence.
the problem of estimating the duration dependence and unobserved heterogeneities in duration data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NPMLE for a discrete duration data model with unobservd heterogeneity and unknown nonparametric duration dependence is a poor estimator of these components of the hazard.

the NPMLE for the discrete duration model is a well behaved estimator when either the duration dependence, the unobserved heterogenity, or both are specified non-parametrically, and that the quasilikelihood estimator with penalty is well behaved in all cases.
the NPMLE is not a reliable estimator of a discrete duration model that allows for nonparametric duration dependence and heterogeneity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonparametric approach to the duration model is not as promising as it might appear at first glance.

the nonparametric specification is a useful and flexible approach to duration analysis, but that the specification of the duration dependence and the unobserved heterogeneities should not be done independently of one another.
, while the NPMLE for discrete duration models is a well behaved estimator, the presence of unobserved heterogeneities and/or nonparametric duration dependence should be treated with caution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NPMLE is a very useful tool for the empirical analysis of duration data.

the NPMLE for a nonparametric discrete duration model with both duration dependence and unobserved heterog eneity is very difficult to use in applied work, even in relatively large samples, because of the difficulty in identifying which of these two features of the model is responsible for a given feature of the data.
the NPMLE is well behaved when the researcher has some knowledge of the data generating process, but can be severely biased when the model is specified nonparametricly.
